findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the 404 path.
findings.body: The test now sends a `state` (`ddd023...`) that does not match the pipeline signature. `OAuthLoginView` therefore rejects the request before `build_integration` runs, so the stubbed 404 for `/app/installations/{id}` is never hit. The old assertion that 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' appears was replaced with the generic state-mismatch message. The test passes without checking the not-found handling it is named for. Use the valid state and stub the OAuth calls (for example with `_stub_github()` followed by the 404 replace). Then step through to the installation and keep the original assertion.

findings.title: Direct indexing of `metadata["sender"]["login"]` can crash with a KeyError.
findings.body: This path runs when an `Integration` row exists but has no `OrganizationIntegration`. A common example is a GitHub integration that was removed from its Sentry org and is now being reinstalled. Rows created through `build_integration`, or before this change, may have no `sender` key in their metadata. `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` then raises a KeyError, and the user gets a 500 page instead of the error dialog. I couldn't see whether every existing row stores `sender`. Read it with `.get()` and send a missing sender to `error(...)`.

findings.title: Error strings passed to `_()` as a variable are no longer picked up for translation.
findings.body:
The short error messages used to be literal `_("GitHub installation pending deletion.")` and `_("Github installed on another Sentry organization.")` calls, so makemessages picked them up for translation. Now plain strings are passed into `error()` and wrapped with `_(error_short)` at runtime. makemessages cannot find strings passed to `_()` through a variable, so these messages and the new default "Invalid installation request." will drop out of the translation catalog.

Fix: wrap the literals with `_()` where they are written (the call sites and the default value) and use `error_short` as given inside `error()`.

held.title: Errors from `get_user_info` are not caught, so the user gets a 500 instead of the error page.
held.body: `get_user_info(access_token)` calls the GitHub `/user` API. If GitHub returns an error or the token is rejected, the helper probably raises (for example an identity or API error) rather than returning a dict without `login`. I could not check how `get_user_info` handles errors. If it does raise, the exception escapes the view and the user sees a 500 instead of the 'Invalid installation request' dialog. Fix: wrap the call in a `try` and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` when it fails.

held.title: Network failures in the token exchange cause a 500 instead of the error page.
held.body: `safe_urlopen` sits outside the `try`. If the call to GitHub's `access_token` endpoint fails with a timeout or connection error, the exception escapes and the user gets a 500 instead of the 'Invalid installation request' dialog. `get_user_info` can also raise when GitHub returns a non-200 response, for example a revoked token. Put both calls inside the try/except and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` when they fail.
